title: A plan the position supports
outcomes: Names the feature of the position that a plan is aimed at
Checks that the pieces can carry the plan out
Recognises a position where a capture decides and no plan is needed

steps.text: A plan is a **direction**, and it needs a reason: a feature of the position to aim at, such as an exposed king, an open file or a weak pawn. Before you commit, ask two questions. **What is the plan aimed at?** And **can my pieces carry it out** before the opponent can stop it?

steps.caption: Black to move. The feature is White's king on g1; the rook and queen are the pieces that can carry the plan.

line.say: Rxg2+: the rook goes to g2 with check, and the queen is ready to join it on the g-file.
Check: the king is hunted and Black mates by force.

steps.text: A plan holds only while its target is there. Move the king and the same attack aims at nothing. As a *rule of thumb*, name the target and the pieces before the first move, and check again after every opponent move. Where a capture or check decides at once, calculate it first; the attack in this lesson was found by calculating, because the target was an exposed king.

steps.title: Same attack, the king has moved
steps.prompt: In the second position White's king stands on b1 instead of g1. Does the plan on g2 survive? Predict first, then check.
Before you chose a move, what was your plan aimed at: a square, a piece or a pawn? Name one plan you considered and dropped, and why. Rate how sure you were (low / medium / high).
